context.brief:
## Employee
- Name: Shamik Bhattacharjee (no id)
- Role: Process Engineer, Process
- Plant / unit: Bengaluru / Unit 100

## Equipment history in the knowledge graph
- none found for this profile; interview from the profile alone and ask them to name their key equipment

topics.title: Core responsibilities and evolution of the Process Engineer role in Unit 100
topics.rationale: Understand undocumented duties, informal expectations, and how the role has changed beyond the official job description.
seed_questions: What were the top three responsibilities that never appeared in your job description?
How did your day-to-day work and priorities shift over the years due to plant changes or management decisions?
Which tasks did you handle that nobody else in the unit could do?

topics.title: Unfinished improvement projects and their current hidden state
topics.rationale: Capture status of incomplete projects, including obstacles, partial implementations, and undocumented decisions.
seed_questions: Which continuous improvement or debottlenecking projects did you leave incomplete, and what is the real blocker?
Are there partially installed equipment or control loops that are not yet commissioned?
What assumptions or test results from these projects exist only in your head or personal notes?

topics.title: Identifying the most critical equipment you own and its undocumented failure modes
topics.rationale: Since the knowledge graph lacks equipment links, prompt the engineer to name key assets and reveal non-documented breakdown patterns.
seed_questions: Which three pieces of equipment in Unit 100 would cause a shutdown tomorrow if they failed—and why is that not in the manuals?
What is the most frequent unplanned failure you dealt with, and what was the real root cause that never got officially recorded?
Are there any recurring seal leaks, vibration issues, or heat exchanger fouling patterns that have no formal troubleshooting guide?

topics.title: Hidden tradeoffs behind past successful process optimizations
topics.rationale: Document side-effects or compromises that came with efficiency gains, which are often omitted from project closeout reports.
seed_questions: Think of a successful yield or energy improvement you made—what side effect did you have to live with that nobody wrote down?
Which operating envelope was tightened so much that operators later found workarounds?
Is there a catalyst or chemical additive change whose long-term effect on downstream equipment is still uncertain?

topics.title: Vendor quirks, unofficial contacts, and support secrets
topics.rationale: Reveal informal relationships and vendor-specific knowledge that speeds up troubleshooting or procurement.
seed_questions: Which equipment vendor do you always call on their personal mobile instead of the support line, and what do they fix that the manual can't?
What unusual spare part substitutions or third-party repairs have you used successfully?
Are there vendor-specific DCS or PLC parameters that are not documented in the system description?

topics.title: Gaps between standard operating procedures and actual practice
topics.rationale: Identify where written SOPs diverge from how things really run, including shortcuts or necessary steps missing from documents.
seed_questions: Which procedure step does every experienced operator skip or modify—and why is it safe (or unsafe) to do so?
Is there a startup or shutdown sequence where the official order is impossible to follow and what is the real sequence?
Where do field operators use 'tribal' valve lineups or bypasses that are not reflected in the P&IDs?

topics.title: Early-warning signs and operator intuition for equipment anomalies
topics.rationale: Capture subtle physical indicators (sounds, vibrations, smells, trends) that predict failures before alarms.
seed_questions: What sound or vibration from a pump or compressor makes you walk over and touch it, even when all readings are normal?
Is there a specific DCS trend or combination of values that always precedes a trip but hasn't been formalized as an alarm?
Which piece of equipment do you mentally 'listen to' at the start of every shift, and what are you checking?

topics.title: Informal cross-department coordination pathways
topics.rationale: Document back-channel communications with maintenance, instrumentation, and utilities that keep the unit running smoothly.
seed_questions: Who is the go-to person in maintenance or I&C that you always call first for a quick fix—and why them?
What is the unwritten process for getting a priority work order through when the CMMS queue is too slow?
Are there recurring conflicts with utilities (steam, cooling water, nitrogen) that you managed through personal relationships?

topics.title: Half-finished trials and unrecorded experimental conclusions
topics.rationale: Capture knowledge from pilot tests or plant trials that were stopped or whose results were never fully documented.
seed_questions: Tell us about a trial run or capacity test that was abandoned—what were the provisional findings?
Which operating condition did you test that gave promising results but was never implemented, and why?
Are there samples or data sets from past experiments stored in your locker or personal drive that nobody else knows about?

topics.title: Non-standard operations during emergencies or unusual events
topics.rationale: Document the real actions taken during past trips, leaks, or utility failures that deviate from written emergency response plans.
seed_questions: Describe the most recent unplanned trip—what was the actual sequence of operator actions that brought it under control, and what did they skip from the written procedure?
Is there a hidden safe operating limit that you know from experience but that is not in the PHA or cause-and-effect matrix?
During a past power failure or steam loss, what critical manual valves had to be moved that are not documented in the blackout procedure?

topics.title: Successor advice and open risk inventory
topics.rationale: Transfer a clear list of immediate risks, pending decisions, and personal advice for the new engineer.
seed_questions: If you had 30 minutes with your replacement, what are the top three things you would tell them to watch out for from day one?
Which equipment or safety system is currently in a degraded state that nobody officially tracks?
What pending management-of-change or HAZOP action items have no clear owner now?

topics.title: Undocumented root causes and fixes from past incidents
topics.rationale: Uncover incident learnings that never made it into official reports or whose corrective actions have latent weaknesses.
seed_questions: Think of a past leak or fire—what was the real chain of events that the investigation report softened, and what should we have fixed but didn't?
Which incident led to a 'temporary' fix that is now permanent, and what is the risk associated with it?
Is there a near-miss that you consider a ticking time bomb, and who knows about it?

topics.title: Equipment adjustments and tuning parameters carried in your head
topics.rationale: Document specific controller tuning constants, relief valve settings, or mechanical adjustments that are not in the asset management system.
seed_questions: Which PID loop tuning values do you keep in a notebook or memory because the last tuning record is wrong?
What spring range or set pressure of a relief valve did you modify in the field without updating the datasheet?
Are there heat exchanger bypass settings or cooling water valve positions that you adjust seasonally and are not written down?

topics.title: Personal lessons learned and career advice for process engineers
topics.rationale: Capture wisdom about professional growth, mistakes to avoid, and how to navigate plant politics.
seed_questions: What is the one technical mistake you made early on that you would tell a junior engineer to never repeat?
How did you build credibility with operators and maintenance techs, and what advice do you have on that?
What skill or knowledge area do you wish you had developed more, and why?

topics.title: Collaboration details with external technology partners or licensors
topics.rationale: Record nuances of working with catalysts, chemicals, or technology suppliers that affect performance but are not in the contract.
seed_questions: Which technology licensor or catalyst supplier gave you technical advice that contradicted the manual—and did it work?
Are there warranty claim or performance guarantee details that are still pending and only you know the history?
What informal arrangement or understanding exists with a chemical supplier about product quality tweaks or delivery flexibility?

transcript.text: Shamik, thank you for sitting down with me today. You've spent years keeping Unit 100 running, and a lot of what you know — the instincts, the lessons, the little things that don't make it into a manual — are only in your head. I want to make sure those don't walk out the door with you. So, let's start broad: looking back at your time here, what is the one thing you'd most want the person stepping into your shoes to understand about Unit 100?
